passages.text: After all these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He laid siege to the fortified cities, intending to conquer them for himself.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah did what was good, upright, and true before the LORD his God.
Hezekiah served God faithfully in all Judah.
After these faithful acts, Sennacherib came.
Sennacherib was king of Assyria.
Sennacherib invaded Judah.
Sennacherib camped against the fortified cities of Judah.
Sennacherib planned to capture these cities for himself.
passages.original: אַחֲרֵ֨י הַדְּבָרִ֤ים וְהָאֱמֶת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה בָּ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּבֹ֣א בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וַיִּ֙חַן֙ עַל־ הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְבִקְעָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come to make war against Jerusalem, he consulted with his leaders and commanders about stopping up the waters of the springs outside the city, and they helped him carry it out.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib came to make war against Jerusalem.
Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had arrived.
Hezekiah knew Sennacherib wanted to attack Jerusalem.
Hezekiah consulted with his leaders.
Hezekiah also consulted with his commanders.
They discussed stopping the waters of the springs outside the city.
The leaders and commanders helped Hezekiah with this plan.
passages.original: וַיַּרְא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּי־ בָ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֑יב וּפָנָ֕יו לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ עִם־ שָׂרָיו֙ וְגִבֹּרָ֔יו לִסְתּוֹם֙ אֶת־ מֵימֵ֣י הָעֲיָנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֣וּץ לָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעְזְרֽוּהוּ׃

passages.text: Many people assembled and stopped up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?” they said.
passages.sermon:
Many people gathered together.
They stopped up all the springs.
They blocked the stream that flowed through the land.
They said, “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?”
passages.original: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ עַם־ רָ֔ב וַֽיִּסְתְּמוּ֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַמַּעְיָנ֔וֹת וְאֶת־ הַנַּ֛חַל הַשּׁוֹטֵ֥ף בְּתוֹךְ־ הָאָ֖רֶץ לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֤מָּה יָב֙וֹאוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמָצְא֖וּ מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: Then Hezekiah worked resolutely to rebuild all the broken sections of the wall and to raise up towers on it. He also built an outer wall and reinforced the supporting terraces of the City of David, and he produced an abundance of weapons and shields.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah saw that Jerusalem was in danger.
Hezekiah became strong and determined.
Hezekiah rebuilt all the broken parts of the city wall.
Hezekiah built towers on the wall.
Hezekiah built another wall outside the first wall.
Hezekiah strengthened the supporting terraces in the City of David.
Hezekiah made many weapons.
Hezekiah made many shields.
passages.original: וַיִּתְחַזַּ֡ק וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַחוֹמָ֨ה הַפְּרוּצָ֜ה וַיַּ֣עַל עַל־ הַמִּגְדָּל֗וֹת וְלַח֙וּצָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֣ה אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק אֶת־ הַמִּלּ֖וֹא עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּ֥עַשׂ שֶׁ֛לַח לָרֹ֖ב וּמָגִנִּֽים׃

passages.text: Hezekiah appointed military commanders over the people and gathered the people in the square of the city gate. Then he encouraged them, saying, “Be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid or discouraged before the king of Assyria and the vast army with him, for there is a greater One with us than with him.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah appointed military commanders over the people.
Hezekiah gathered the people to himself.
Hezekiah brought them to the square at the city gate.
Hezekiah spoke to encourage their hearts.
Hezekiah said, “Be strong.
Be courageous.
Do not be afraid.
Do not be discouraged because of the king of Assyria.
Do not be discouraged because of the large army with him.
There is a greater One with us than with him.”
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֛ן שָׂרֵ֥י מִלְחָמ֖וֹת עַל־ הָעָ֑ם וַיִּקְבְּצֵ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו אֶל־ רְחוֹב֙ שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר עַל־ לְבָבָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ אַל־ תִּֽירְא֣וּ וְאַל־ תֵּחַ֗תּוּ מִפְּנֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמִלִּפְנֵ֖י כָּל־ הֶהָמ֣וֹן אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ עִמָּ֥נוּ רַ֖ב מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles.” So the people were strengthened by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah spoke to the people of Judah.
Hezekiah said, “With him is only the arm of flesh.
With us is the LORD our God.
The LORD our God helps us.
The LORD our God fights our battles.”
The people trusted the words of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
The people became strong.
passages.original: עִמּוֹ֙ זְר֣וֹעַ בָּשָׂ֔ר וְעִמָּ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ לְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ וּלְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמֹתֵ֑נוּ וַיִּסָּמְכ֣וּ הָעָ֔ם עַל־ דִּבְרֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Later, as Sennacherib king of Assyria and all his forces besieged Lachish, he sent his servants to Jerusalem with a message for King Hezekiah of Judah and all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem: “This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What is the basis of your confidence, that you remain in Jerusalem under siege?
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He had many forces with him.
He was attacking the city of Lachish.
After this, Sennacherib sent his servants to Jerusalem.
He sent them with a message.
He sent this message to Hezekiah, king of Judah.
He sent it to all the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
Sennacherib said, “This is what the king of Assyria says.
Why are you so confident?
Why do you stay in Jerusalem while it is under siege?”
passages.original: אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח סַנְחֵרִ֨יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֤וּר עֲבָדָיו֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלַ֔יְמָה וְהוּא֙ עַל־ לָכִ֔ישׁ וְכָל־ מֶמְשַׁלְתּ֖וֹ עִמּ֑וֹ עַל־ יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַל־ כָּל־ יְהוּדָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֔ר סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר עַל־ מָה֙ אַתֶּ֣ם בֹּטְחִ֔ים וְיֹשְׁבִ֥ים בְּמָצ֖וֹר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Is not Hezekiah misleading you to give you over to death by famine and thirst when he says, ‘The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria?’
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He sent a message to the people of Jerusalem.
He spoke about Hezekiah, the king of Judah.
He asked the people a question.
He said, “Is not Hezekiah misleading you?”
He said, “Hezekiah tells you that the LORD our God will deliver you from the hand of the king of Assyria.”
He said, “Hezekiah is giving you over to death.”
He said, “You will die by famine and thirst.”
He said these things to make the people doubt Hezekiah’s words.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֤א יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ מַסִּ֣ית אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָתֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָמ֛וּת בְּרָעָ֥ב וּבְצָמָ֖א לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ יַצִּילֵ֕נוּ מִכַּ֖ף מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Did not Hezekiah himself remove His high places and His altars and say to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before one altar, and on it you shall burn sacrifices’?
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah is the king of Judah.
Hezekiah removed the high places.
Hezekiah took away the altars.
Hezekiah spoke to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
Hezekiah said, “You must worship before one altar.”
Hezekiah said, “You must burn sacrifices on this one altar.”
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ הוּא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הֵסִ֥יר אֶת־ בָּמֹתָ֖יו וְאֶת־ מִזְבְּחֹתָ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה וְלִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לִפְנֵ֨י מִזְבֵּ֧חַ אֶחָ֛ד תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ וְעָלָ֥יו תַּקְטִֽירוּ׃

passages.text: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Have the gods of these nations ever been able to deliver their land from my hand?
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib spoke to the people of Judah.
Sennacherib said, "Do you not know what I have done?
My fathers and I have acted against all the peoples of the lands.
We have conquered many nations.
The gods of these nations could not save their lands from my hand.
No god has delivered any land from me."
passages.original: הֲלֹ֣א תֵדְע֗וּ מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֙יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י וַאֲבוֹתַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל עַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת הֲיָכ֣וֹל יָֽכְל֗וּ אֱלֹהֵי֙ גּוֹיֵ֣ הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־ אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction has been able to deliver his people from my hand? How then can your God deliver you from my hand?
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib spoke to the people of Judah.
He reminded them about his fathers.
His fathers destroyed many nations.
He asked a question about the gods of those nations.
He said, “Who among all the gods of these nations my fathers destroyed was able to save his people from my hand?”
He challenged the people of Judah.
He said, “How can your God save you from my hand?”
passages.original: מִ֠י בְּֽכָל־ אֱלֹהֵ֞י הַגּוֹיִ֤ם הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱרִ֣ימוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָכ֔וֹל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־ עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִ֑י כִּ֤י יוּכַל֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: So now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him mislead you like this. Do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you from my hand!”
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
Hezekiah is your king.
Do not let Hezekiah deceive you.
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you in this way.
Do not believe Hezekiah.
No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save his people from my hand.
No god has saved anyone from the hand of my fathers.
Your God will not save you from my hand.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה אַל־ יַשִּׁיא֩ אֶתְכֶ֨ם חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאַל־ יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֣ם כָּזֹאת֮ וְאַל־ תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ לוֹ֒ כִּי־ לֹ֣א יוּכַ֗ל כָּל־ אֱל֙וֹהַ֙ כָּל־ גּ֣וֹי וּמַמְלָכָ֔ה לְהַצִּ֥יל עַמּ֛וֹ מִיָּדִ֖י וּמִיַּ֣ד אֲבוֹתָ֑י אַ֚ף כִּ֣י אֱ‍ֽלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹא־ יַצִּ֥ילוּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: And the servants of Sennacherib spoke further against the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib had servants.
These servants spoke.
They spoke against the LORD God.
They also spoke against Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the servant of the LORD God.
passages.original: וְעוֹד֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ עֲבָדָ֔יו עַל־ יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He also wrote letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel, and saying against Him: “Just as the gods of the nations did not deliver their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver His people from my hand.”
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib wrote letters.
He mocked the LORD, the God of Israel, in these letters.
He spoke against the LORD in his words.
He said, “The gods of the nations did not save their people from my hand.
In the same way, the God of Hezekiah will not save His people from my hand.”
passages.original: וּסְפָרִ֣ים כָּתַ֔ב לְחָרֵ֕ף לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֵֽאמֹ֨ר עָלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֵּֽאלֹהֵ֞י גּוֹיֵ֤ הָאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־ הִצִּ֤ילוּ עַמָּם֙ מִיָּדִ֔י כֵּ֣ן לֹֽא־ יַצִּ֞יל אֱלֹהֵ֧י יְחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: Then the Assyrians called out loudly in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them in order to capture the city.
passages.sermon:
The Assyrians wanted to capture Jerusalem.
They spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
The people stood on the city wall.
The Assyrians called out in Hebrew.
They shouted with loud voices.
They wanted to frighten the people.
They wanted to terrify them.
They did this so they could take the city.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ בְקוֹל־ גָּד֜וֹל יְהוּדִ֗ית עַל־ עַ֤ם יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה לְיָֽרְאָ֖ם וּֽלְבַהֲלָ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן יִלְכְּד֥וּ אֶת־ הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: They spoke against the God of Jerusalem as they had spoken against the gods of the peoples of the earth—the work of human hands.
passages.sermon:
The Assyrians spoke against the God of Jerusalem.
They treated Him like the gods of other nations.
Those other gods were made by people.
The Assyrians thought the God of Jerusalem was just like those man-made gods.
passages.original: וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־ אֱלֹהֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כְּעַ֗ל אֱלֹהֵי֙ עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם׃ס

passages.text: In response, King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz cried out to heaven in prayer, and the LORD sent an angel who annihilated every mighty man of valor and every leader and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he withdrew to his own land in disgrace. And when he entered the temple of his god, some of his own sons struck him down with the sword.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah ruled Judah.
Isaiah was a prophet and the son of Amoz.
The Assyrian army threatened Jerusalem.
King Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed to God about this danger.
They cried out to heaven for help.
The LORD heard their prayer.
The LORD sent an angel.
The angel destroyed every mighty warrior in the Assyrian camp.
The angel also destroyed every leader and commander there.
The king of Assyria saw his army defeated.
He returned to his own land in shame.
He entered the temple of his god.
His own sons killed him there with the sword.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֞ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וִֽישַֽׁעְיָ֧הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֛וֹץ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל־ זֹ֑את וַֽיִּזְעֲק֖וּ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ וַיַּכְחֵ֞ד כָּל־ גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֙יִל֙ וְנָגִ֣יד וְשָׂ֔ר בְּמַחֲנֵ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּשָׁב֩ בְּבֹ֨שֶׁת פָּנִ֜ים לְאַרְצ֗וֹ וַיָּבֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהָ֔יו וּמִיצִיאוֹ מֵעָ֔יו שָׁ֖ם הִפִּילֻ֥הוּ בֶחָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the hands of King Sennacherib of Assyria and all the others, and He gave them rest on every side.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
The people of Jerusalem lived under his rule.
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib attacked Jerusalem.
The LORD saved Hezekiah from Sennacherib.
The LORD saved the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib.
The LORD saved them from all their enemies.
The LORD gave them peace on every side.
passages.original: וַיּוֹשַׁע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־ יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאֵ֣ת׀ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם מִיַּ֛ד סַנְחֵרִ֥יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֖וּר וּמִיַּד־ כֹּ֑ל וַֽיְנַהֲלֵ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב׃

passages.text: Many brought offerings to Jerusalem for the LORD and valuable gifts for Hezekiah king of Judah, and from then on he was exalted in the eyes of all nations.
passages.sermon:
Many people brought offerings to the LORD.
They brought these offerings to Jerusalem.
Many people also brought valuable gifts to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
After these things, all nations honored Hezekiah.
All nations saw him as exalted.
passages.original: וְ֠רַבִּים מְבִיאִ֨ים מִנְחָ֤ה לַיהוָה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּמִ֨גְדָּנ֔וֹת לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנַּשֵּׂ֛א לְעֵינֵ֥י כָל־ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מֵאַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵֽן׃ס

passages.text: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. So he prayed to the LORD, who spoke to him and gave him a sign.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah became very sick.
Hezekiah was close to death.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Hezekiah.
The LORD gave Hezekiah a sign.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ עַד־ לָמ֑וּת וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ וּמוֹפֵ֖ת נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But because his heart was proud, Hezekiah did not repay the favor shown to him. Therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
God showed favor to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah became proud in his heart.
Hezekiah did not repay the favor God showed him.
God’s wrath came upon Hezekiah.
God’s wrath also came upon Judah.
God’s wrath also came upon Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ כִגְמֻ֤ל עָלָיו֙ הֵשִׁ֣יב יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ וַיְהִ֤י עָלָיו֙ קֶ֔צֶף וְעַל־ יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart—he and the people of Jerusalem—so that the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them during the days of Hezekiah.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah became proud in his heart.
Hezekiah humbled himself.
The people of Jerusalem also humbled themselves.
They humbled their pride.
The LORD did not send His wrath on them.
This happened during the days of Hezekiah.
passages.original: וַיִּכָּנַ֤ע יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־ בָ֤א עֲלֵיהֶם֙ קֶ֣צֶף יְהוָ֔ה בִּימֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Hezekiah had very great riches and honor, and he made treasuries for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable articles.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah had very great riches.
Hezekiah had much honor.
Hezekiah made treasuries for himself.
Hezekiah stored silver in these treasuries.
Hezekiah stored gold in these treasuries.
Hezekiah stored precious stones in these treasuries.
Hezekiah stored spices in these treasuries.
Hezekiah stored shields in these treasuries.
Hezekiah stored all kinds of valuable articles in these treasuries.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאֹֽצָר֣וֹת עָֽשָׂה־ ל֠וֹ לְכֶ֨סֶף וּלְזָהָ֜ב וּלְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֗ה וְלִבְשָׂמִים֙ וּלְמָ֣גִנִּ֔ים וּלְכֹ֖ל כְּלֵ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה׃

passages.text: He also made storehouses for the harvest of grain and new wine and oil, stalls for all kinds of livestock, and pens for the flocks.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah made storehouses.
He made these storehouses for grain.
He made them for new wine.
He made them for oil.
Hezekiah also made stalls.
He made stalls for all kinds of livestock.
He made pens for the flocks.
passages.original: וּמִ֨סְכְּנ֔וֹת לִתְבוּאַ֥ת דָּגָ֖ן וְתִיר֣וֹשׁ וְיִצְהָ֑ר וְאֻֽרָוֺת֙ לְכָל־ בְּהֵמָ֣ה וּבְהֵמָ֔ה וַעֲדָרִ֖ים לָאֲוֵרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He made cities for himself, and he acquired herds of sheep and cattle in abundance, for God gave him very great wealth.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah made cities for himself.
Hezekiah acquired many herds of sheep.
Hezekiah acquired many herds of cattle.
God gave Hezekiah very great wealth.
passages.original: וְעָרִים֙ עָ֣שָׂה ל֔וֹ וּמִקְנֵה־ צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר לָרֹ֑ב כִּ֤י נָֽתַן־ לוֹ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים רְכ֖וּשׁ רַ֥ב מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the Spring of Gihon and channeled it down to the west side of the City of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all that he did.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah blocked the upper outlet of the Spring of Gihon.
Hezekiah directed the water down to the west side of the City of David.
Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did.
passages.original: וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ סָתַם֙ אֶת־ מוֹצָ֞א מֵימֵ֤י גִיחוֹן֙ הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן וַֽיַּישְּׁרֵ֥ם לְמַֽטָּה־ מַּעְרָ֖בָה לְעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּצְלַ֥ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכָֽל־ מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

passages.text: And so when ambassadors of the rulers of Babylon were sent to him to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land, God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah’s heart.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
The rulers of Babylon sent ambassadors to Hezekiah.
These ambassadors came to ask about the wonder that happened in the land.
God left Hezekiah alone at that time.
God did this to test Hezekiah.
God wanted to know everything that was in Hezekiah’s heart.
passages.original: וְכֵ֞ן בִּמְלִיצֵ֣י׀ שָׂרֵ֣י בָּבֶ֗ל הַֽמְשַׁלְּחִ֤ים עָלָיו֙ לִדְרֹ֗שׁ הַמּוֹפֵת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ לָדַ֖עַת כָּל־ בִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his deeds of loving devotion, they are indeed written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was a king of Judah.
Hezekiah did many acts.
Hezekiah showed loving devotion in his deeds.
The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, wrote about Hezekiah.
Isaiah wrote these things in his vision.
These records are in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים בַּחֲז֞וֹן יְשַֽׁעְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־ אָמוֹץ֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא עַל־ סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Hezekiah rested with his fathers and was buried in the upper tombs of David’s descendants. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death. And his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah died.
People buried Hezekiah in the upper tombs of David’s descendants.
All Judah honored Hezekiah when he died.
The people of Jerusalem also honored Hezekiah at his death.
Manasseh was Hezekiah’s son.
Manasseh became king after Hezekiah.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻהוּ֮ בְּֽמַעֲלֵה֮ קִבְרֵ֣י בְנֵי־ דָוִיד֒ וְכָבוֹד֙ עָֽשׂוּ־ ל֣וֹ בְמוֹת֔וֹ כָּל־ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
